raffles-gruendet-singapur#text: During the Napoleonic Wars the British had occupied Java, and Raffles was its governor from 1811 to 1816. When the Netherlands got their colonies back, he looked for a new base and in 1819 concluded a treaty with a claimant to the throne of Johor. Singapore became a free port and grew rapidly, above all through Chinese immigration. In the Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 the two powers divided their spheres of interest along the Strait of Malacca; in 1826 Penang, Malacca and Singapore were combined into the Straits Settlements. From 1874 protectorate treaties also brought the sultanates of the Malay Peninsula under British control, where tin and later rubber became important exports.
anglo-birmanische-kriege#summary: In three wars Britain conquers the kingdom of the Konbaung dynasty and incorporates Burma into British India in 1886.
anglo-birmanische-kriege#text: Konbaung expansion into Assam and Manipur led to conflict with the British East India Company. In the First War of 1824 to 1826 Burma had to cede Assam, Manipur, Arakan and Tenasserim in the Treaty of Yandabo and pay a large indemnity. In 1852 the British occupied Lower Burma with Rangoon. King Mindon founded Mandalay as his new capital in 1857 and tried to modernize his kingdom cautiously. In the Third War of 1885 British troops took Mandalay and sent King Thibaw into exile in India; on 1 January 1886 Burma became a province of British India. Resistance groups fought the occupation for years afterwards.
dekabristenaufstand#summary: Noble officers in St Petersburg refuse to swear allegiance to the new Tsar Nicholas I and demand a constitution; the revolt is crushed the same day.
dekabristenaufstand#text: Many young officers had come to know Western Europe in the wars against Napoleon and founded secret societies that sought a constitution and the end of serfdom. When Tsar Alexander I died in November 1825 and the succession was briefly unclear, on 14 December by the Julian calendar they led about 3,000 soldiers onto Senate Square in St Petersburg. Nicholas I had artillery fire on them; an uprising in Ukraine also failed a few weeks later. Five leaders, among them Pavel Pestel and Kondraty Ryleyev, were hanged in 1826, and more than a hundred were exiled to Siberia, where some of their wives followed them. The Decembrists became a model for later revolutionaries.
java-krieg-und-kultursystem#title: The Java War and the Cultivation System
java-krieg-und-kultursystem#summary: After the bloody uprising of Prince Diponegoro, the Netherlands force the peasants of Java to grow export crops for the colonial state.
java-krieg-und-kultursystem#text: In 1825 Prince Diponegoro of the royal house of Yogyakarta rose against Dutch rule and the colonial administration's influence over the court. The war lasted five years and, according to estimates, cost the lives of well over 100,000 Javanese; in 1830 Diponegoro was taken prisoner during negotiations and exiled. In the same year Governor-General Johannes van den Bosch introduced the Cultivation System: villages had to devote part of their land or working time to coffee, sugar and indigo, which the state bought at fixed prices. The Netherlands earned enormous sums from it, while famines struck Java in the 1840s. After criticism, for example in the novel Max Havelaar, the system was gradually dismantled from 1870.
novemberaufstand-in-polen#summary: Polish officer cadets spark an uprising against Russian rule in Warsaw, which is crushed after almost a year of war.
novemberaufstand-in-polen#text: In 1815 the Congress of Vienna had created a Kingdom of Poland whose king was the Russian tsar; at first it had its own constitution and army. Because Nicholas I disregarded these rights, officer cadets stormed the Belweder in Warsaw, the residence of Grand Duke Constantine, on 29 November 1830. In 1831 the Sejm declared the tsar deposed, but the Russian army recaptured Warsaw in September. The constitution was abolished, the universities of Warsaw and Vilnius were closed, and thousands went into the Great Emigration to Western Europe, among them the poet Adam Mickiewicz. The January Uprising of 1863, which spread across Poland, Lithuania and Belarus, also failed and was followed by harsh Russification.
vertrag-von-waitangi#summary: British officials and Māori chiefs sign a treaty that becomes the basis of the colony of New Zealand – its meaning is disputed to this day.
vertrag-von-waitangi#text: On 6 February 1840 at Waitangi on the Bay of Islands, the British representative William Hobson and some 40 chiefs signed the treaty; by September more than 500 further signatures had been added across the country, though some large tribes did not sign. According to the English text the Māori ceded sovereignty to the British Crown; according to the Māori version, which most of them signed, they ceded only "kāwanatanga", a form of governorship, while being guaranteed "tino rangatiratanga", full authority over their lands, villages and treasures. Britain then claimed all of New Zealand, which became a separate colony in 1841. Since 1975 the Waitangi Tribunal has investigated breaches of the treaty, which is regarded as the country's founding document.
neuseelandkriege#summary: In a series of wars, Māori tribes fight British troops and colonial militias over land and self-determination.
neuseelandkriege#text: From 1844 the chief Hōne Heke had repeatedly cut down the British flagstaff at Kororāreka in the north; in March 1845 his warriors attacked the settlement, and the first war began. The largest conflicts broke out over land: in Taranaki in 1860 and in the Waikato in 1863/64, where the government attacked the King Movement. Māori defended themselves in ingenious pā with trenches and rifle pits, but in the end were overwhelmed by a superior force of more than ten thousand soldiers. Under a law of 1863 the government confiscated more than a million hectares of Māori land. The last fighting against the followers of Te Kooti ended in 1872.
goldrausch-in-australien#summary: Gold discoveries in New South Wales and Victoria trigger mass immigration and transform the colonies.
goldrausch-in-australien#text: In February 1851 Edward Hargraves found gold near Bathurst in New South Wales, and a few months later rich finds followed at Ballarat and Bendigo in Victoria. Tens of thousands of immigrants from Britain, Ireland, continental Europe, North America and China poured onto the goldfields; within a decade the population of Victoria rose from under 80,000 to over half a million. Anger over expensive mining licences led in 1854 to the rebellion at the Eureka Stockade near Ballarat, which was bloodily suppressed but brought reforms in its wake. At the same time hostility grew towards Chinese miners, who were subjected to special taxes and attacked.
maori-koenigsbewegung#title: Founding of the Māori King Movement
maori-koenigsbewegung#summary: Several tribes choose Pōtatau Te Wherowhero as the first Māori king in order to halt further land sales.
maori-koenigsbewegung#text: In the 1850s concern grew among Māori that more and more land was being lost to settlers. After several large gatherings, tribes mainly from the Waikato and the central North Island chose the elderly chief Pōtatau Te Wherowhero as king in 1858; the chief Wiremu Tāmihana was the movement's leading advocate. The king was to unite the tribes and protect land from sale without rejecting the British queen. The colonial government, however, saw this as a challenge to its rule, which contributed to the war in the Waikato in 1863. The Kīngitanga still exists today.
aufhebung-der-leibeigenschaft-in-russlan: The Abolition of Serfdom in Russia
Tsar Alexander II frees some 23 million serfs; they become personally free but have to pay dearly for their land.

Defeat in the Crimean War had shown how far Russia lagged behind economically and militarily. Alexander II declared that it was better to abolish serfdom from above than to wait for it to abolish itself from below. With the manifesto of 19 February 1861 by the Julian calendar, privately owned serfs received personal freedom and the right to marry, acquire property and go to court. The land they worked, however, they had to redeem over 49 years with payments to the state, and they often received less than before; taxes and land remained tied to the village commune. Reforms of the courts, of local self-government in the zemstvos and of the army followed.
verkauf-alaskas#summary: Russia sells its American colony to the United States for 7.2 million dollars.
verkauf-alaskas#text: In 1741 the expedition of the Dane Vitus Bering, in Russian service, had reached the coast of Alaska. Fur traders followed the hunt for sea otters, and from 1799 the Russian-American Company administered the colony, from 1808 out of Novo-Arkhangelsk, today's Sitka; Aleuts and other indigenous peoples were forced to hunt for it. After the Crimean War the remote territory, which was hard to defend, was considered a burden, especially as fur stocks had dwindled. In March 1867 both sides signed the purchase treaty, and in October the American flag was raised in Sitka. In the United States critics at first mocked the purchase; only gold strikes and later oil revealed the value of the land.
coming-of-the-light-torres-strait#title: "Coming of the Light" in the Torres Strait
coming-of-the-light-torres-strait#summar: Missionaries of the London Missionary Society land on the island of Erub; Torres Strait Islanders still celebrate the day as the arrival of Christianity.
coming-of-the-light-torres-strait#text: The Torres Strait Islanders between Australia and New Guinea lived from gardening, fishing and sea trade and had their own languages, ceremonies and canoe networks reaching as far as the coast of New Guinea. On 1 July 1871 missionaries of the London Missionary Society, among them Samuel Macfarlane, landed on Erub (Darnley Island) together with teachers from the Loyalty Islands. Many islanders adopted Christianity and combined it with their own traditions; 1 July is celebrated as the "Coming of the Light". At the same time pearl-shell diving and the sea-cucumber trade brought outside workers and traders to the region, which was annexed to the colony of Queensland in 1872 and 1879.
verfassung-von-tonga#summary: King George Tupou I gives Tonga a written constitution which, in amended form, is still in force and secures the country as an independent monarchy.
verfassung-von-tonga#text: Tāufaʻāhau, a chief from Haʻapai, was baptized by Methodist missionaries in 1831 and took the name George. After years of civil war he united Tonga and in 1845 became ruler of the whole country as Tuʻi Kanokupolu. He issued law codes, freed commoners from dependence on the chiefs in 1862 and on 4 November 1875 gave Tonga a constitution with a parliament and basic rights. It prohibited the sale of land to foreigners and helped Tonga avoid colonization; in 1900 it merely became a British protectorate and kept its monarchy.
emser-erlass#summary: Tsar Alexander II bans the printing and import of most books in the Ukrainian language in the tsarist empire.
emser-erlass#text: The authorities of the tsarist empire regarded Ukrainians as part of a single Russian people and their language as a dialect. As early as 1863 a circular from Interior Minister Valuev had banned Ukrainian school and religious books. In May 1876, in the spa town of Bad Ems, Alexander II signed a secret decree that prohibited, with few exceptions, the printing of Ukrainian books, their import from abroad, and Ukrainian theatre performances and song lyrics. Ukrainian writers and scholars then moved their work to Austrian Galicia, with Lviv as its centre. The restrictions lost their force only after the Revolution of 1905.
gruendung-franzoesisch-indochinas#summar: France combines Cochinchina, Annam, Tonkin and Cambodia into the Indochinese Union; Laos is added in 1893.
gruendung-franzoesisch-indochinas#text: In 1858 French and Spanish ships attacked Đà Nẵng, ostensibly to protect persecuted missionaries. In 1862 the Nguyễn court had to cede three southern provinces, which became the colony of Cochinchina, and in 1863 Cambodia became a French protectorate. In 1883 and 1884 Annam and Tonkin also became protectorates, and in the war of 1884/85 China had to renounce its suzerainty over Vietnam. In 1887 the Indochinese Union was created under a governor-general, and Laos was added in 1893. France built railways and plantations and financed the administration through monopolies on opium, salt and alcohol. Resistance to the conquest included the Cần Vương movement in the name of the young emperor Hàm Nghi.
bau-der-transsibirischen-eisenbahn#summa: Russia builds a railway more than 9,000 kilometres long from Moscow to Vladivostok on the Pacific.
bau-der-transsibirischen-eisenbahn#text: In May 1891 the heir to the throne, Nicholas, laid the foundation stone in Vladivostok; the project was driven forward by Finance Minister Sergei Witte. Tens of thousands of workers, among them convicts and soldiers, built several sections at once through taiga, swamps and permafrost. From 1904 it was possible to travel all the way to the Pacific, at first via a shortcut through Manchuria; the route entirely on Russian territory was completed in 1916 with the bridge over the Amur at Khabarovsk. The railway opened Siberia to millions of settlers and to mining and agriculture and strengthened Russia's position in East Asia, which contributed to the war with Japan in 1904/05.
paknam-krise-siam#title: The Paknam Crisis: Siam Keeps Its Independence
paknam-krise-siam#summary: French gunboats force their way to Bangkok; Siam cedes territory east of the Mekong but remains the only independent state in Southeast Asia.
paknam-krise-siam#text: In July 1893 French gunboats forced their way past the fortress at Paknam and up the Chao Phraya to Bangkok. King Chulalongkorn had to cede the territories east of the Mekong, today's Laos, to France and pay an indemnity. In 1896 Britain and France agreed to respect Siam's heartland as a buffer state between their colonies; later Siam gave up further territory in Cambodia and on the Malay Peninsula. Mongkut had already opened trade with the Bowring Treaty of 1855; from 1868 Chulalongkorn built up ministries, schools, an army and railways on European lines and gradually abolished slavery. In this way Siam avoided colonial rule, though at the price of territorial losses.
sturz-der-monarchie-hawaii#summary: American businessmen, backed by US Marines, overthrow Queen Liliʻuokalani.
sturz-der-monarchie-hawaii#text: From the mid-19th century planters and businessmen of American descent dominated Hawaiʻi's sugar economy; in 1887 they forced on King Kalākaua a constitution that curtailed his power and tied the right to vote to property. When his sister and successor Liliʻuokalani sought to proclaim a new constitution in 1893, a group of them formed a "Committee of Safety" and on 17 January declared a provisional government after Marines from a US warship had come ashore. The queen yielded to superior force to avoid bloodshed and appealed to the US government. President Grover Cleveland condemned the overthrow, but its leaders proclaimed the Republic of Hawaiʻi in 1894.
philippinische-revolution#summary: The secret society Katipunan rises against Spain; in 1898 the Philippines proclaim independence but come under the rule of the United States.
philippinische-revolution#text: In 1892 Andrés Bonifacio founded the Katipunan in Manila, which aimed to win independence by force of arms. When it was discovered in August 1896, the uprising began. The Spanish had the writer José Rizal, who had not himself called for armed struggle, shot on 30 December 1896. In internal power struggles Emilio Aguinaldo prevailed, Bonifacio was executed in 1897, and at the end of 1897 Aguinaldo went into exile after an agreement with Spain. During the Spanish-American War he returned in 1898 and proclaimed independence on 12 June. In the Treaty of Paris, however, Spain ceded the Philippines to the United States, against which the Filipinos fought a costly war from 1899.
annexion-hawaiis#summary: By a resolution of Congress, Hawaiʻi becomes part of the United States – against the protests of many Hawaiians.
annexion-hawaiis#text: An annexation treaty had failed to win the required two-thirds majority in the Senate, partly because of petitions signed by more than 20,000 Hawaiians. During the Spanish–American War Hawaiʻi gained importance as a base on the route to the Philippines, and in July 1898 Congress approved annexation by a joint resolution, which needed only simple majorities. On 12 August 1898 the Hawaiian flag was lowered in Honolulu; in 1900 Hawaiʻi became a US territory and in 1959 the 50th state. In 1993 the US Congress formally apologized for the overthrow of 1893.
australische-foederation#summary: On 1 January 1901 the six Australian colonies unite as the Commonwealth of Australia.
australische-foederation#text: After constitutional conventions in the 1890s, voters in the colonies approved a common constitution in referendums, which the British Parliament confirmed in 1900. On 1 January 1901 the federation was proclaimed in Sydney; Edmund Barton became the first prime minister, and parliament sat provisionally in Melbourne. Australia remained part of the British Empire but managed its own internal affairs. One of the first federal laws, the Immigration Restriction Act of 1901, laid the foundation of the "White Australia" policy; Aboriginal people were largely passed over in the constitution and were not included in the federal population count until 1967.
revolution-von-1905#summary: After Bloody Sunday in St Petersburg, strikes, peasant unrest and mutinies sweep the tsarist empire; Nicholas II has to concede a representative assembly, the Duma.
revolution-von-1905#text: Defeats in the war against Japan sharpened discontent over hunger, working conditions and lack of rights. On 9 January 1905 by the Julian calendar a peaceful procession of workers led by the priest Georgy Gapon marched to the Winter Palace to present a petition to the tsar; soldiers fired into the crowd and killed hundreds of people. Strikes followed throughout the empire, including in Poland, the Baltic and the Caucasus, along with peasant revolts and the mutiny on the battleship Potemkin. After a general strike, Nicholas II promised civil rights and an elected Duma in the October Manifesto. He nevertheless kept sweeping powers, soon dissolved the first Dumas, and Prime Minister Pyotr Stolypin had insurgents harshly prosecuted.
februarrevolution-1917#summary: Strikes and bread riots in Petrograd, joined by the garrison, force Nicholas II to abdicate; the rule of the Romanovs comes to an end.
februarrevolution-1917#text: The First World War cost millions of soldiers their lives and brought shortages to the cities. On International Women's Day, 23 February 1917 by the Julian calendar and 8 March by today's calendar, women textile workers went on strike in Petrograd, as St Petersburg had been called since 1914; within days the protests grew into a general strike, and soldiers went over to the demonstrators. Members of the Duma formed a Provisional Government, and workers and soldiers formed the Petrograd Soviet. On 2 March (15 March) Nicholas II abdicated, and his brother Michael declined the crown. In Kyiv the Ukrainian Central Rada was formed that same month. How the Bolsheviks took power in the autumn is described in the event of the Russian Revolution.
